A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LVTINO research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original Adobe240 restoration experiments, quantitative comparisons in Table 1, component ablations in Table 3, and qualitative reconstruction examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds original GoPRO240 results, runtime and memory measurements, noise tests, scheduling ablations and nonlinear restoration examples.

M1.justification: The VCM/ICM/TV splitting, CausVid and DMD2 backbones, and LVTINO/LVTINO-V update procedures are retained. Flow-LVTINO is discussed as a future extension; the nonlinear experiments do not document a new solver component.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on 239 GoPRO240 test clips, supplementing Adobe240. Appendix A.7 also adds a higher-noise scenario and a nonlinear task combining Gaussian noise with JPEG compression. GoPRO240 appeared in v1 only as the initialization network's training source.

E2.justification: VIDUE becomes an explicit Problem C comparator in v2 Tables 1, 2 and 6, whereas v1 used its network only for initialization. VISION-XL and ADMM-TV remain. BiM-VFI appears in a separate diagnostic comparison against VIDUE in Figure 7, rather than a direct LVTINO benchmark.

E3.justification: v1 Table 2 becomes v2 Table 4 with revised settings for all three problems: A's temporal TV weight changes from 0.005 to 2.8e-4 and both proximal coefficients from 1e5 to 1e6; B's coefficients change from (1e5, 2e3) to (3e3, 1.5e5); C's spatial TV weights change from 1e-4 to 1e-6. New experiments introduce timing and parameter-sweep protocols. These reported revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The original TV and ICM ablations are retained as v2 Table 5. New Appendix A.7 adds noise robustness testing, step-size/regularization sensitivity heatmaps, VCM/ICM scheduling ablations, residual error maps, and a BiM-VFI-versus-VIDUE case study examining motion-blur handling.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without experimental seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added tables and sensitivity heatmaps do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Original Adobe240 and component-ablation numerical entries are retained, while v2 adds substantial results for GoPRO240, noise, computational cost, scheduling and JPEG restoration. The new VIDUE entry achieves FVMD 142.5 versus LVTINO's 602.5 on Adobe240 Problem C. Table 3 reports LVTINO at 132 seconds and 35.15 GB versus VISION-XL at 176 seconds and 15.64 GB.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.5 adds a formal flow-matching setup, derives the flow-induced denoiser's MMSE identity in Equations 11–12, states straight-flow exact-recovery conditions, and develops the PnP-Flow iteration in Equations 13–14. This substantially expands the mathematical treatment, drawing on prior work; the original Langevin derivation remains and no new LVTINO convergence proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims: a first VCM-based zero-shot/PnP solver for high-definition video restoration, combining temporal coherence and spatial detail with few evaluations and no automatic differentiation. Added experiments support these retained contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive discussion of runtime-memory tradeoffs, nonlinear applicability conditional on evaluating the likelihood proximal operator, and robustness inferred from the new analyses. It also identifies restricted pretrained timesteps as a limitation on tuning eta and discusses error accumulation in long-video generation.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code/project-access statement, changes video links from Streamable to GitHub, identifies the A100 timing hardware, specifies bicubic ×8 upsampling for VIDUE, and documents additional scheduling configurations. The hyperparameter table is revised, while the existing forward-operator and proximal-solver implementation descriptions are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix A.5 adds an extended relationship to Martin et al.'s PnP-Flow and supporting flow-matching/PnP literature. v2 also positions the work relative to concurrent zero-shot restoration, task-specific video restorers, DiffIR2VR and recent long-video generation research, substantially expanding the prior-work discussion.

P1.justification: Most original prose and the main section sequence remain. Changes include conference headers, limited wording edits, condensation of the numerical-stability discussion into a footnote, and insertion of new appendix subsections with updated cross-references.

P2.justification: v2 adds four tables covering GoPRO240, computational costs, noise and scheduling, plus four figures showing baseline diagnostics, JPEG restoration, sensitivity heatmaps and error maps. Table 1 gains a VIDUE row, and main qualitative figures are consolidated. Original appendix Figures 7–12 are retained as Figures 11–16.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the unchanged method: the second benchmark, VIDUE comparison, noise/compression tests and sensitivity analyses address v1's limited evidence of generalization and robustness. Actual runtime and memory measurements make efficiency claims assessable beyond NFE counts. Unexplained hyperparameter revisions alongside unchanged scores and Table 7's inconsistent task label limit reproducibility, but the gains in validation and transparency clearly outweigh these caveats.
